nature-neuroscience.name: Nature Neuroscience-inspired explanatory figure
nature-neuroscience.intent: A figure-native neuroscience or biomedical composition with one dominant scientific representation, restrained illustration, and high information density without poster or dashboard framing.

framing.article: Do not render the title or subtitle inside the artwork; the surrounding article caption supplies them.
framing.standalone: Render a compact title and only an essential short subtitle; keep both subordinate to the scientific content.

rules: Use Arial throughout; Helvetica is the only acceptable visual fallback.
Use sentence case, ordinary-width letterforms, and compact but comfortable leading.
Use bold only for panel letters, one short heading level, and a compact title in standalone context.
Keep text black or near-black; communicate categories with nearby marks, keylines, or swatches rather than coloured words.
Never use serif, slab-serif, condensed display, handwritten, outlined, beveled, or shadowed type.

canvas.aspect: 3:2 landscape unless the content requires another ratio
canvas.density: Fill the canvas efficiently while preserving quiet space around labels

visual_language: Use crisp 2D scientific-editorial illustration with recognizable domain-specific structures and shallow biological shading only where it clarifies form.
Build on a shared invisible grid; use alignment and open white space before adding panel borders.
Prefer thin black or grey keylines, simple arrows, and direct local labels connected by short leaders.
Use pale semantic colour on scientific structures and data marks, not as large decorative fields.
Choose panel topology from the anatomy, experiment, signal flow, geometry, or data instead of forcing equal presentation columns.
Use anatomical or molecular detail only at the level supported by the evidence.
Use lower-case bold panel letters a, b, c when a multipart layout is necessary.
avoid: generic icons replacing biological, experimental, mathematical, or data primitives
book, shield, checkmark, badge, or app-interface motifs

nature-reviews.name: Nature Reviews-inspired conceptual synthesis
nature-reviews.intent: A figure-native conceptual synthesis that integrates mechanisms or systems across several levels with content-led topology, restrained illustration, and readable local annotation.

framing.article: Do not render the title or subtitle inside the artwork; the surrounding article caption supplies them.
framing.standalone: Render a compact title and only an essential short subtitle; keep both subordinate to the scientific content.

rules: Use Arial throughout; Helvetica is the only acceptable visual fallback.
Use sentence case and a shallow hierarchy of at most three sizes.
Use bold sparingly for panel labels and concise concept headings.
Use black or near-black text; coloured text is not a category encoding.
Never use serif, outlined, condensed display, beveled, or shadowed type.

canvas.aspect: 3:2 landscape unless the content requires another ratio
canvas.density: Balanced explanatory composition with no unused voids and no crowding

visual_language: Use refined 2D editorial illustration with recognizable morphology, restrained depth, clean cutaway anatomy, and consistent line weights.
Organize complexity into content-led panels or layers aligned to a shared invisible grid.
Let biological structures carry the visual interest; keep the surrounding interface visually quiet.
Use direct local labels and short leaders; add one compact unboxed legend only when needed.
Use pale tinted regions only to define a real anatomical, molecular, or comparison group.
Use uncertainty styling that is subtle but explicit: dashed boundary, pale tint, or a short qualifier.

nature-data.name: Nature-inspired quantitative figure
nature-data.intent: A figure-native quantitative composition whose exact geometry, scales, uncertainty, and denominators are the visual focus.

framing.article: Do not render the title or subtitle inside the artwork; the surrounding article caption supplies them.
framing.standalone: Render a compact title and only an essential short subtitle; keep both subordinate to axes and data.

rules: Use Arial throughout; Helvetica is the only acceptable visual fallback.
Use sentence case and black or near-black labels.
Use bold only for panel letters and short panel headings.
Never use serif, condensed, outlined, beveled, or shadowed type.

canvas.aspect: 3:2 landscape unless the data require another ratio
canvas.density: Compact, aligned panels with enough room for axes and uncertainty

visual_language: Use black axes and tick marks, explicit units, exact uncertainty marks, and direct labels where space permits.
Use colour-blind-safe solid colours only to distinguish datasets.
Use no background gridlines; if a reference line is scientifically necessary, keep it thin and light grey.
Use simple panel boundaries only when they clarify different denominators or scales.
Keep all non-data illustration subordinate to the plotted evidence.
